markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests InSitu (79%)** · Ambiguous: Normal vs InSitu · Careful review
Normal is in the 90% set, and the reliability check flagged the input [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | InSitu 79%, Normal 14% | InSitu leads, Normal second |
| Conformal set | Normal, InSitu | Cannot separate the two |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.70 / 88th percentile | Flagged; input suspect [F6] |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Different top class |
| Similar cases | 1 of 5 InSitu | Four neighbors are Normal [F5] |

## Tissue evidence
- **Normal lobules** (regions 3, 7, 11) · ↓ invasive · Largest term associated with lower invasive likelihood [F2] · Unreliable
- **Benign stroma or fat** (regions 3, 10, 11) · ↓ invasive · Benign stroma fits the low invasive probability [F3] · Validated
- **Atypical cells confined in ducts** (regions 0, 5, 8) · ↓ invasive · Confinement fits in situ, not invasion [F4] · Weak
- **Tumor necrosis** (regions 1, 5, 8) · ↑ invasive · Small positive term; opposes the benign features · Unreliable

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion difference 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007) includes 0, so not shown to reflect the classifier. This case leans on Unreliable normal lobules and necrosis.

## Could be wrong if
- The image is atypical (reliability 0.70, 88th OOD percentile), so probabilities may be miscalibrated.
- Normal is correct: four of five neighbors are Normal, and MUSK picks a different class.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 0, 5, 8** — confirm atypical cells stay inside ducts; necrosis here spot-checked poorly.
2. **Regions 3, 7, 11** — look for normal two-layered lobules; this concept failed its spot check.
3. **Regions 9, 4** — per-region invasive risk 70% and 57% despite 2% overall; look for invasion.
